posts.text: A town in Oklahoma tried to charge $17,000 to provide a local farmer with documents and records about his arrest at a Townhall meeting on data center construction. Daren Blanchard was arrested when he went 30 seconds over his allotted time. He pleaded not guilty and asked for public records and body cam footage. The city tried to charge him $17,000 for those records, but the state of Oklahoma called that some unlawful.
posts.summary: Criticizes excessive public records fees as retaliation for speech

posts.text: Is the NYPD paying Muslim officers an hour every day to go pray at a mosque? According to @@IMRIGHTINFRONT3it is true. But it doesn’t: New York City is simply following federal law Title VII and Supreme Court orders to provide “reasonable accommodations“ for sincerely, Held, religious beliefs. The rule doesn’t require anyone to pay employees, but simply to accommodate their religious beliefs and applies to all religions, not just Islam.
posts.summary: Defends NYPD religious accommodation as compliance with federal law

posts.text: Trump announced that the United States secured a deal for $65 billion of oil from Venezuela. Is that accurate, like @Political Education says? The deal isn’t quite like that. The agreement gives a private company rights of access to oil fields in Venezuela and the United States government will secure the loans needed for that company to operate in exchange for profit-sharing, if any, and the ability to buy some of that oil at cost.
posts.summary: Fact-checks Trump Venezuela oil deal claim, clarifies actual structure
